proposed_changes.after: Resolution 726-23 imposes a one-year moratorium from July 15, 2026, effective immediately upon passage. Its completed certification-of-action blocks show clerk and mayor approval. The previously reviewed July 15 minutes record adoption by nine affirmative votes with two commissioners absent. The executed text and original term are now available; VERIFY later amendments, waiver decisions, termination or replacement, litigation and present legal force.

New data centers and significant expansions in every zoning district of unincorporated Hamilton County. Section 1 bars accepting, processing, approving or issuing zoning map/text amendments, site/development plans, building permits and other approvals that authorize or vest rights. Section 2 literally specifies projected peak electric demand of "1 MW" or refusal to disclose demand, together with electronic equipment and environmental-control criteria; it does not print "at least" or "more than" 1 MW. Section 4 exempts lawfully existing operating centers (routine maintenance/repairs without increased capacity or impacts) and projects with final, unappealable vested rights before effectiveness. Section 7 prohibits circumvention and section 8 allows Commission-reviewed waivers. Actual project applicability is unverified.

facts.value: Hamilton County, Tennessee, Resolution No. 726-23, approving and authorizing a data-center moratorium.
facts.supporting_quote: No. 726-23 ... A RESOLUTION APPROVING AND AUTHORIZING A MORATORIUM ON DATA CENTERS IN THE UNINCORPORATED AREAS OF HAMILTON COUNTY, TENNESSEE.

facts.value: The certification of action has the county-clerk approval and county-mayor approval boxes checked, signatures on both lines, and the date July 15, 2026; the rejection and veto boxes are unchecked.
facts.supporting_quote: Approved: ... County Clerk ... Approved: ... County Mayor ... July 15, 2026

facts.value: The resolution takes effect immediately upon passage. The moratorium runs for one year from adoption unless extended, shortened, or terminated earlier by further Commission resolution. The document is dated July 15, 2026; its one-year calendar anniversary is July 15, 2027.
facts.locator: Physical page 1, date; physical page 2, section 6; physical page 3, section 9 and certification
facts.supporting_quote: This moratorium shall be effective for one (1) year from the date of adoption of this Resolution, unless extended, shortened, or terminated earlier by further resolution ... This Resolution shall take effect immediately upon its passage

facts.value: A Data Center is a business that primarily operates both electronic equipment used to process, store, or transmit digital information and the environmental control equipment necessary to maintain proper operating conditions for that equipment, and that either is projected to have a peak electric demand of 1 MW or refuses to disclose its peak electric demand level. The text says '1 MW,' not 'at least 1 MW.'
facts.supporting_quote: Primarily operates: a) electronic equipment used to process, store, or transmit digital information; and b) environmental control equipment necessary to maintain proper operating conditions for the said electronic equipment; and c) (i) said business is projected to have a peak electric demand of 1 MW; or (ii) said business refuses to disclose its peak electric demand level

facts.value: The moratorium covers new data centers and significant expansions of existing data centers throughout unincorporated Hamilton County in all zoning districts. The County may not accept, process, approve, or issue the specified zoning amendments, plans, permits, or other approvals that would authorize or vest rights for construction, operation, or significant expansion.
facts.supporting_quote: the County shall not accept, process, approve, or issue any zoning map amendments, zoning text amendments, site plans, development plans, building permits, or any other approvals or permits that would authorize or vest rights ... This moratorium applies throughout the unincorporated areas of Hamilton County and to all zoning districts.

facts.value: Exemptions cover lawfully existing data centers operating in unincorporated areas as of the effective date, with routine maintenance and repairs that do not increase capacity or impacts permitted; and projects that obtained final, unappealable vested rights under applicable Tennessee law before the effective date.
facts.supporting_quote: Lawfully existing Data Centers operating in the unincorporated areas of Hamilton County as of the effective date ... routine maintenance and repairs that do not increase capacity or impacts are permitted ... Any project that has obtained final, unappealable vested rights under applicable Tennessee law prior to the effective date

facts.value: The Planning Department must study impacts, develop zoning recommendations, engage stakeholders, and present written findings and proposed zoning text and/or map amendments to the Commission by March 1, 2027, or an earlier date directed by the Commission.
facts.supporting_quote: Prepare and present written findings and proposed zoning text and/or map amendments to the Hamilton County Commission no later than March 1, 2027, or such earlier date as the Commission may direct

facts.value: The Commission may extend, shorten, or terminate the moratorium earlier by further resolution. It retains authority to modify or lift it after favorable action on Planning Department recommendations or a determination that sufficient permanent regulations have been adopted.
facts.supporting_quote: The Commission retains full authority to modify the terms of this moratorium or lift it upon receipt and favorable action on recommendations from the Planning Department or upon a determination that permanent regulations have been adopted and are sufficient.

facts.value: Any entity may apply for a waiver through the Planning Department. The Commission reviews it and may grant it if deemed necessary for the County's general health or welfare.
facts.supporting_quote: Any entity may apply for a waiver ... through the Hamilton County Planning Department that shall be reviewed by the Hamilton County Commission and may be granted if it is deemed necessary for the general health or welfare of the County.

facts.value: Circumvention is prohibited, including fragmentation into smaller facilities or phases, reclassification of uses, or other actions intended to avoid the prohibitions.
facts.supporting_quote: No person or entity shall circumvent the intent of this moratorium by, for example, fragmenting projects into multiple smaller facilities or phases, reclassifying uses, or taking other actions intended to avoid the prohibitions herein.

facts.value: The retained July 15, 2026 minutes report unanimous adoption of Resolution 726-23, 9–0, with two members absent.
facts.supporting_quote: to adopt Resolution No. 726-23 ... The foregoing Motion was unanimously adopted on a Roll Call vote ... Total present – 9. Total absent – 2. Total “Aye” votes – 9. Total “Nay” votes – 0.
